input: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling

team.claim: Founders: Parker Conrad (CEO) and Prasanna Sankar; launched 2016, HQ San Francisco.

Parker Conrad previously founded Zenefits (2013) and resigned as Zenefits CEO in Feb 2016 amid a compliance scandal; Prasanna Sankar (ex-Zenefits director of engineering) left Rippling in 2021 to start 0xPPL; Albert Strasheim joined as CTO in Aug 2022.

Current executives per Rippling's own about page (company claim): Parker Conrad CEO; Matt MacInnis President & CPO; Matt Plank CRO; Albert Strasheim CTO; Adam Swiecicki CFO; Martin White General Counsel; Bridget Abraham Chief Compliance Officer.

The Information org chart (last updated Apr 15, 2025): Parker Conrad Co-Founder/CEO; Prasanna Sankar co-founder and board member; Matt MacInnis COO; Eisar Lipkovitz Chief Product Officer; Matt Plank CRO; Vanessa Wu General Counsel.
Board: Mamoon Hamid (Kleiner Perkins), Napoleon Ta (Founders Fund), Parker Conrad, Prasanna Sankar; Coatue took an observer seat in 2024 (aggregator/org-chart data).

New hires (company claim): Wan Agus joined as SVP Engineering, IT Products (previously CTO at Credit Karma); Gang Wang joined as SVP Engineering, Finance Products (previously CTO at Nuvei, earlier Stripe and Intuit).
Mrinal Chatterjee (former Walmart executive) appointed India country head in 2024, overseeing the Bengaluru office.

Notable departure (last 2 years): Adil Syed — joined as CFO in 2019, later SVP Global & GTM for Tech and head of CorpDev/IR/Partnerships — announced farewell after seven years (LinkedIn post ~Oct 2026).
Notable departure: Chris Campbell, Deputy General Counsel, left Rippling after five years (LinkedIn post ~Oct 2026); legal team had grown from 2 to 30 people during his tenure.
Notable departure: Sinead Smyth left after nearly 3 years as CRO of Rippling Payments Ireland, joining Trading 212 Money Europe as CRO (~Sept 2026).
Notable departure: Keith O'Brien, Global Payroll Compliance Manager in Dublin (employed June 2023–March 2025), exited after being exposed as Deel's paid spy and confessing in a sworn affidavit.

funding.claim: Total raised to date: $1.85 billion (TechCrunch, May 2025); CB Insights (aggregator) lists $1.849B over 14 rounds.
Seed: $7M raised March 2017; Y Combinator Winter 2017 batch.
Series B: $145M led by Founders Fund; Series A: $45M (per company blog related-posts listing).
Series C: $250M led by Sequoia Capital Global Equities & Global Growth with Greenoaks participation; valued $6.5B as of the October 2021 round (company blog listing + Contrary).
Series D: $250M co-led by Bedrock and Kleiner Perkins, with Y Combinator and Sequoia participation, valuing the company at $11.25 billion.
Series E: $500M led by Greenoaks (March 2023), with CapitalG, Lightspeed and others (CB Insights); valuation $11.25B (Reuters).

Series F: $200M led by Coatue at a $13.5B valuation, announced Apr 22, 2024, with a separate tender offer of up to $590M from employees and early investors; Founders Fund's $310M commitment was its largest single-round check ever; Dragoneer joined as new investor.

Series G: $450M announced May 9, 2025, valuing the company at $16.8 billion; no lead investor; participants include Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives/Growth, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator, plus existing investors; alongside a tender offer repurchasing up to $200M of employee equity (company claim, confirmed by Reuters/TechCrunch).

Aggregator estimate: AG Dillon lists the last primary round valuation as $17.5B (May 2025) — conflicts with the company's stated $16.8B; implied valuation $16.9B as of Nov 2, 2026 with secondary pricing 3.2% below last round.
IPO: CEO Parker Conrad says an IPO is not planned in the near future and the company would need to be profitable first; Reuters notes tender offers are likely to become an annual event.

output.verdict: Rippling looks strong on breadth and scale: 20+ products spanning HR, payroll, IT and finance on a single data graph, 20,000+ customers including Y Combinator, ~$1B claimed annualized revenue, and a $16.8B Series G valuation (May 2025) with $1.85B total raised. Closer look needed at: (1) the ongoing Deel espionage litigation — Rippling's RICO claims survived dismissal in Feb 2026, but Deel's countersuit raises contested Russia-sanctions and compliance allegations; (2) the ~600 layoffs across Jan–Mar 2026 that clash with the headcount-growth narrative; and (3) the cluster of 2026 executive departures (ex-CFO/CorpDev lead, Deputy GC, Payments Ireland CRO) versus the company's own claims.

business.claim: Sells an integrated HR/Payroll/IT/Finance SaaS platform ('Everything HR, Payroll, IT, and Finance teams need in one system'): HRIS, benefits, PEO, recruiting, performance, US & global payroll, Employer of Record, contractor management, identity & access, device management, corporate cards, bill pay, travel, expense management, banking, App Studio.

Business model: chiefly SaaS subscription fees, plus transactional revenue — FX earnings on payroll/bill payments, float income, interchange from corporate card swipes, and revenue share from third parties like Google Workspace and 401(k) partners (company claim).
Fintech structure: 'Rippling is a fintech company, not a bank' — checking accounts and banking services provided by Column N.A., Member FDIC (company claim).

Targets customers from startups to mid-sized enterprises with up to 10,000 employees across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; 2024 Reuters reporting said it targets companies with fewer than 2,000 workers.

Geographies: HQ San Francisco; offices listed in SF, NYC, Austin, Seattle, London, Dublin, Bengaluru, Sydney, Toronto, Singapore; global products 'work across 185+ countries and 50+ currencies'; Employer of Record in ~80 countries (company claims).
India is Rippling's largest office outside San Francisco; India workforce grew from 450 to 1,000+ in a year with plans to double to 2,000 over three years (company claim).
Regulated subsidiaries with licenses: Rippling Insurance Services (NPN 18578689), Rippling PEO 1 Inc. (FL License GL250), Rippling Payments Inc. (NMLS 1931820), Rippling Lending Inc. (NMLS 2430865).
Per its own court complaint: Delaware corporation with principal place of business in San Francisco, founded 2016, serving 'tens of thousands of customers around the world'.

traction.claim: Company claim: over 20,000 customers as of May 2025 (also stated to Reuters and SiliconANGLE).
Company claim: works with over 15,000 startups including Cursor (Anysphere), Clay and Sierra.
Y Combinator became a Rippling customer in early 2025 and called it the HR 'tool of choice' for its founders; Rippling offers a discounted 'Founder Mode' offer for YC-funded companies.
Company claim: named customers include Five Guys, Taskrabbit, Anthropic, Barry's, Clay, Blank Street Coffee, Superhuman, Chess.com, Highnoon, Compass Coffee and Qualio.
Company claim (aggregator-cited): PEO business had 99.5% y/y client retention as of fall 2024; 10+ product lines each over $1M ARR.
Company claim via CNBC: employee scheduling tool launched in October became its fastest product to reach $1M in sales; launched Talent Signal, an AI tool analyzing new hires' work performance.

Partnerships: became an Apple Business Partner (Jan 15, 2026, after becoming an Apple Authorized Reseller Aug 2025); Duffel powers Rippling Travel (July 2025); Sigma360 partnership for sanctions screening (PR Newswire).
CEO claim: publicity from the Deel lawsuit may be boosting business — some companies said they were talking to Rippling because of it.

Acquired Reprompt AI (reported Nov 6, 2026) to extend AI capabilities from answering questions to executing work; terms undisclosed. Earlier acquired Fuzzbuzz (Apr 25, 2023) and made a $5M seed investment in Lorikeet (Oct 2024) per CB Insights.

red_flags.claim: ~600 employees laid off across four events Jan–Mar 2026 (100 on Jan 29; 200 on Feb 28; 100 on Mar 21; 200 on Mar 29, 2026 — first large-scale layoffs, per The Information/TechCrunch via SecretRemote, aggregator), reversing the 'no recent layoffs' position of June 2025 and the 6,000+ headcount claim of Oct 2026.

Bilateral litigation with Deel: Rippling's RICO/trade-secret suit (Mar 2025) and Deel's countersuit (Apr 2025) alleging Rippling violated Russia sanctions, is not tax compliant, and defrauds employees and customers — all denied by Rippling in a court filing.

Internal security/insider exposure: Rippling's own complaint discloses that its systems were compromised for four months by a payroll compliance manager spying for Deel, and that two other former employees allegedly downloaded sensitive data before joining Deel.
Founder's prior record: SEC fined Parker Conrad $533K (and Zenefits $450K) in 2017 over misleading investors at his previous company — a regulatory-history item, not a Rippling action.

Secondary-market valuation softness: shares trading ~3.2% below the last primary round as of Nov 2, 2026 (AG Dillon aggregator estimate); also an aggregator valuation of $17.5B that conflicts with the company's stated $16.8B.
Unverified anonymous Blind posts (Jan 2026) claim India head Mrinal Chatterjee resigned to eBay and that the chief security officer left — anecdotal, not corroborated by any named source.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor (aggregator): overall rating 3.6/5 from 1,313 reviews; 66% would recommend to a friend; rating decreased 3% over the last 12 months; 74% positive business outlook.
Glassdoor category ratings (aggregator): CEO Parker Conrad approval 79%; Compensation 3.9, Career opportunities 3.8, Culture & values 3.4, Senior management 3.4, Work/Life balance 3.0.
Complaint patterns (Glassdoor reviews/summary, aggregator): burnout, low work-life balance, micromanagement, understaffed support teams, high turnover, poor benefits (e.g., no 401k match).
Demographic rating gaps on Glassdoor (aggregator): Black or African American 2.8 stars (19 ratings), Hispanic or Latinx 2.9 (27), Women 3.3 (98), LGBTQ+ 2.8 (32), Transgender/Non-Binary 2.2 (8).
Blind (aggregator): company rating 3.2/5 from 585 reviews; recent posts complain about Rippling India engineering culture and work-life balance (anecdotal).

Company claim: awards/ratings — Fast Company 2026 'Next Big Thing in Tech', G2 '#1 AI Agent for HR', TrustRadius Top Rated 2026, Software Advice and Capterra 4.9-star ratings; CNBC named Rippling to its Disruptor 50 list (ranked 14th in 2023).

Critical press context: Deel's spokesperson called Rippling's allegations 'far fetched' and said Rippling 'has a long history of making false or sensationalized allegations to governmental authorities about competitors' (contested competitor claim).
Marketing-controversy precedent: in early 2020 Rippling ran ads targeting Gusto customers ('Outgrowing Gusto? Presto Change-o.'); Gusto sent a cease-and-desist and Rippling took the ads down.

missing_fields: Formal regulatory enforcement action against Rippling (none identified; only Deel's contested Russia-sanctions allegation, denied by Rippling)
Deel countersuit court docket (not located; countersuit known only via press)
Systematic customer complaint data (only employee-review aggregators and anecdotal forum posts found)

financial_signals.claim: ARR more than doubled in 2023 to over $350M, per The Information (estimate, cited by SiliconANGLE and CNBC).
Annualized revenue reached $570M, per sources who spoke to The Information (estimate); Inc. cited a $580M estimate in March 2025 (estimate).
Sacra estimate (aggregator): $1B annualized revenue as of March 2026, up from $850M at end of 2025, growing 78% y/y.
Company claim via departing exec Adil Syed's own LinkedIn post (~Oct 2026): Rippling has grown to over 6,000 global employees and over $1B in annualized revenue with high growth.
Benzinga (May 27, 2026): revenue scale near $1 billion; steady demand in secondary markets, closely watched as a potential pre-IPO company.
Company claim (CEO): annual revenue growth 'well over 30%'; not profitable and prioritizing top-line growth over profitability.
Company claim (CEO, Apr 2024): revenue doubled year-over-year; unprofitable but sitting on over $1 billion cash; headcount 2,800 across US, India, Ireland, UK and Australia.
Headcount trend (company claims): 2,800 (Apr 2024) -> 4,000+ (May 2025) -> 5,000+ (Jan 2026, 'more than 90 percent of Rippling's 5,000+ employees use Mac computers') -> 6,000+ (Oct 2026 claim).

Layoffs 2026 (aggregator SecretRemote citing The Information and TechCrunch): ~100 employees Jan 29, 2026 (restructuring); 200 on Feb 28; 100 on Mar 21; 200 on Mar 29, 2026 — described as its first large-scale layoffs, totaling ~600.
CNBC (June 2025): Rippling 'has not had recent layoffs' — contrast with the Jan–Mar 2026 cuts.
Hiring signal (company claim): India workforce grew 450 -> 1,000+ in one year; plans to reach 2,000 in India within three years; Glassdoor listed 440 open US jobs as of 2026-11-09 (aggregator).
Aggregator estimate: secondary-market implied valuation $16.9B (Nov 2, 2026), 3.2% below last round; was -7.5% in Oct 2026 — a softness signal.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Rippling filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal. (Case 3:25-cv-02576) against Deel on Mar 17, 2025, alleging RICO violation and conspiracy, federal/California trade-secret misappropriation, tortious interference, aiding and abetting breach of fiduciary duty, and unfair competition — claiming Deel cultivated a spy inside Rippling for over four months (primary source: court-record complaint).

Complaint alleges the spy searched 'Deel' ~23x/day for four months and searched Slack 6,000+ times, capturing sales pipeline, pricing and battlecards; Rippling Ireland obtained an emergency Irish High Court preservation order on Mar 12, 2025, with penal endorsement; the spy allegedly refused and fled the Dublin office.

Former Rippling employee Keith O'Brien confessed in an affidavit made public in an Irish court (Apr 2, 2025) to spying for Deel CEO Alex Bouaziz for ~€5,000/month; communications were on auto-deleting Telegram; payments routed via the Revolut account of Deel COO's wife, then shifted to Ethereum at Philippe Bouaziz's direction (Reuters + First Amended Complaint).

First Amended Complaint filed Jun 5, 2025 (N.D. Cal., Judge Charles R. Breyer) directly names Deel CEO Alex Bouaziz, chairman/CFO Philippe Bouaziz and COO Dan Westgarth; Rippling's amended suit calls it the 'Bouaziz Racketeering Enterprise' / 'criminal syndicate' and claims at least four corporate victims (primary source: FAC PDF).

Company claim: on Feb 25, 2026 Judge Breyer rejected Deel's attempt to dismiss; civil RICO and trade-secret claims move forward against Deel and its top executives toward trial; court found plausible predicate acts of obstruction of justice, wire fraud and trade-secret theft.

Company claim (Rippling blog links): a Mar 25, 2026 post says Deel faces sanctions motions for obstructing court orders and admits paying the spy; a May 1, 2026 post says the spy was paid $6,000/month in crypto for 'high-value watches' until March 2025.

Deel countersued Rippling on Apr 25, 2025 for alleged defamation, libel and deceptive trade practices, claiming Rippling violated sanctions regarding payments into Russia, is not tax compliant, and defrauds employees and customers (Deel claims, contested).

Rippling denies the sanctions allegations in its own court filing: it states it 'has never transmitted sanctioned payments to Russia' and alleges Deel's senior counsel instructed the spy to make a false sanctions-related complaint (primary source: FAC PDF).

No regulatory enforcement action against Rippling was identified in searches as of 2026-11-09; the Russia-sanctions claim appears only as a Deel allegation that Rippling denies (Business Insider noted the allegation and Rippling's denial).

Founder history (prior company, not Rippling): in October 2017 the SEC fined Parker Conrad $533K and Zenefits $450K over misleading investors; Conrad settled without admitting wrongdoing (relates to Zenefits).
